instruction: I made venmo payment requests to some of my friends yesterday evening. Unfortunately, I have made a mistake in calculation. Each of them owes me $15 less than the requested amount. So delete those requests and make new ones with everything else the same, but with the corrected amount.
notes: Two apps: supervisor and venmo. The agent must list its sent payment requests, pick the ones created yesterday evening (2023-05-19, evening hours, status pending), delete each and recreate it with the same recipient, description and privacy but amount reduced by 15. The problem models two such requests (the real number is only known at runtime; add more payment-request/person/email objects and extend the goal and complete-task parameters if more are found). Static init facts (request-to, person-email, request-amount, request-description, request-privacy) describe the structure of the original requests; they only become usable after venmo.show_sent_payment_requests sets (sent-requests-listed), which models the lookup. The $15 correction is encoded by the static (fifteen-less new old) relation between amount objects rather than numeric fluents. Since all requests shared the same dinner share, a single amount pair is used. supervisor.complete_task takes the two request records as non-API parameters so its precondition can enforce that every request has been deleted and recreated; it is called with no API arguments. The reference solution reportedly had 9 calls (likely an extra listing/pagination call); the plan here uses 8.

plan: (venmo-create-payment-request email-friend-1 amount-requested-minus-15 venmo-token description-yesterday-request privacy-yesterday-request request-friend-1 friend-1 amount-requested)
(venmo-create-payment-request email-friend-2 amount-requested-minus-15 venmo-token description-yesterday-request privacy-yesterday-request request-friend-2 friend-2 amount-requested)
